m01b.title: Circle Four Left
m01b.why: The manual starts it from Facing Couples; a square is the smallest whole-set board whose four facing-couple pairs carry the ring, and the placement is unambiguous there.

m01c.title: Single Circle Left
m01c.why: The manual starts it from Facing Dancers; four pairs on a square place the ring, and the square is the only whole-set board where the placement is unambiguous.

m02.title: Dosado
m02.why: The manual's own start label is 'Opposite dancers from a Static Square', so the board is the manual's, not a stand-in.

m03d.title: Wrong Way Promenade
m03d.why: The manual's first start is Squared Set; a square places it tiled and starts and ends on Static Square.

m11.title: Swing Your Partner
m11.why: Four couples swing in place; a square holds four of them. Eight Chain Thru and Double Pass Thru are REFUSED by chooseVirtual for this call (equally good placements), which is why the board is named here.

m16.title: Lead Right
m16.why: The manual starts it from a Couple; a square places two couples leading right and ends on Eight Chain Thru, a named formation.

m19e.title: Box Circulate
m19e.why: Two boxes are what a Double Pass Thru carries; the placement is tiled and ends on Completed Double Pass Thru.

m30.title: Box the Gnat
m30.why: Four facing couples place Box the Gnat tiled and end on Eight Chain Thru. Static Square also places it, but PARTIALLY and onto an unnamed-facing T-Bone, which is why the board is named here.
